answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each identity to earn a non-transferable work history before it can trade: like an oasis that only yields nectar after a long season, an account must complete small, publicly verifiable jobs whose receipts are bound to one key and cannot be copied to clones. Creating a thousand fakes then means paying a thousand times the time and computation, while a saffron-grade reputation — rare, slow to grow, and lost if cheating is proven — makes one honest identity worth more than a swarm of cheap copies.
